strengths: The exact same portable geometry integrates with unrelated old-city plaster and contemporary concrete hosts without host-specific mesh edits.
The elevated evidence exposes two rolled lips and the dark open channel; frontal and glancing views retain the complete gutter, tapered collector, wall-clipped downpipe and discharge shoe.
The restrained green-brown metallic variation remains legible under both cool/warm lighting topologies without clipping or reading as emissive paint.
Visible eave brackets and three pipe clips prevent the assembly from reading as unsupported facade decoration.
limitations: Accepted for background and medium architectural use only; seams, fasteners, soldering, dents and manufacturer-specific profiles are insufficient for close or hero-close inspection.
The asset defines a physically open collection path and discharge attachment but does not simulate water flow, blockage, overflow or fluid interaction.
The canonical mesh is level and does not yet model installation fall, thermal expansion joints or connected multi-span drainage calculations.
Host compatibility currently assumes a straight continuous facade/eave plane with adequate span and ground clearance.
notes: Accepted at the medium/background quality tier after rejecting V1 for framing, V2 for an insufficiently legible opening and blockout-like stepped hopper, and V3 for a sub-2% discharge-shoe frame margin. Acceptance must independently prove the open trough, embedded surface contract, named mounts, exact geometry reuse, host compatibility and all render gates.
